questions.text: In an encoder–decoder transformer, where do the queries, keys, and values for decoder cross-attention come from?

options.A: Queries and keys come from the encoder; values come from the decoder.
options.B: Queries, keys, and values all come from the decoder hidden states.
options.C: Queries come from the decoder; keys and values come from encoder outputs.
options.D: Queries come from the encoder; keys and values come from decoder states.

questions.explanation: Decoder cross-attention uses decoder states to query the encoded source, which provides the keys and values.

questions.text: You adapt an encoder–decoder block into a standard GPT-style decoder-only block. Which change preserves the intended architecture?

options.A: Remove cross-attention; retain causal self-attention and the feed-forward sublayer.
options.B: Remove causal self-attention; retain cross-attention and the feed-forward sublayer.
options.C: Remove the feed-forward sublayer; retain cross-attention and unmasked self-attention.
options.D: Remove the causal mask; retain cross-attention to an empty encoder output.

questions.explanation: A standard decoder-only block omits encoder cross-attention while retaining causal self-attention, an FFN, normalization, and residual connections.

questions.text: Which expression implements a pre-norm residual sublayer?
questions.explanation: Pre-norm normalizes the input to the sublayer and adds its output back to the unchanged residual input x.
